a: Throughout history, many brilliant women have made groundbreaking contributions to science, mathematics, and technology, yet their names remain largely unknown. Rosalind Franklin was a British chemist and X-ray crystallographer whose work was critical to understanding the molecular structures of DNA, RNA, and viruses, yet she was not awarded the Nobel Prize that her male colleagues received. Lise Meitner was an Austrian-Swedish physicist who co-discovered nuclear fission, but she was excluded from the 1944 Nobel Prize in Physics awarded to her colleague Otto Hahn. Chien-Shiung Wu was a Chinese-American physicist who conducted the famous Wu experiment that proved the violation of parity conservation in weak interactions, a discovery that earned her male colleagues the 1957 Nobel Prize in Physics. Jocelyn Bell Burnell was a Northern Irish astronomer who discovered the first radio pulsars in 1967, yet she was not included in the Nobel Prize awarded to her advisor Antony Hewish. Nettie Stevens was an American biologist who discovered the chromosomal basis of sex determination (the XY system), but her discovery was overshadowed by that of Edmund Beecher Wilson, who published similar findings around the same time. Esther Lederberg was an American biochemist who developed the technique of replica plating and made significant contributions to bacterial genetics, but she was often overshadowed by her Nobel Prize-winning husband Joshua Lederberg. Miriam Benjamin was an American educator and inventor who developed a system of moving chairs for public transportation and was the first African American woman to patent a game, yet her contributions to education and invention are rarely mentioned. These women, along with many others like Ada Lovelace, Henrietta Leavitt, and Vera Rubin, made discoveries that fundamentally changed our understanding of the universe, yet their stories are often omitted from history books. Their exclusion from recognition reflects the systemic barriers that women have faced in scientific fields throughout history.
